study.title: Psalm 62 Rest, trust, and judgment in God
study.overview: This psalm presents David amid the pressure of adversaries, but without losing the spiritual serenity. He begins by stating that his soul finds rest in God, describes the instability and falsehood of enemies, and then calls the people to trust the Lord at all times. In the final part, the psalm confronts the illusion of trusting people, violence or riches, and ends with a solemn conviction: God has power, goodness and also judges every person according to his works.

outline.title: The soul quieted in the face of the threat
outline.explanation: David declares that his security comes from God, not from the circumstances. Although there are attacks, conspiracies, and deceitful words, he sees the adversaries as fragile before the Lord. The contrast between trust in God and human instability is presented right at the beginning.

outline.title: Reinforcement of personal trust and public call
outline.explanation: David's own heart is again called to rest in God. He repeats that the Lord is his rock, salvation, glory, strength, and refuge, and then extends the exhortation to the people: trust in God at all times and pour out his heart before him.

outline.title: The vanity of human resources and the certainty of divine judgment
outline.explanation: Psalm teaches that people, oppression and riches do not deserve final confidence. God spoke with authority, is the source of power and also of goodness, and repays each one according to his work.

study.context: The notes indicate that the psalm was associated with David and handed over to the regent "for Jedutum." The exact historical episode is not informed with certainty, but the text reflects a situation of real danger, with political opposition and language that suggests an attempt to overthrow the king for lies and betrayal. The commentators understand that there was a threat of usurpation and instability around David.
study.theology: Psalm teaches a theology of exclusive trust in God. The soul finds rest when submitting to the Lord and waiting for him, rather than reacting with fear or self-reliance. God is described as rock, salvation, refuge, strength, glory, and hope, which shows that security, identity, and hope proceed from him. In contrast, the human being is a passenger, deceptive and unable to sustain ultimate trust. The text also states that power belongs to God and that his goodness does not contradict his judgment: he repays according to works. Thus grace, sovereignty, and justice appear united in the divine character.

scholarViews.insight: The psalm expresses confidence in the king, who rests in God despite the difficulties; his adversaries seem strong, but they are fragile, passengers and deceitful in the light of God.
David presents his dependence on God as something calm and persevering; his soul is quiet and waits in the Lord, submitting to what God has.
Enemies want to overthrow David from his elevated position through falsehood and cunning, using words of loyalty while planning evil.

questions: In which areas do you need, like David, to send your soul to settle before God instead of reacting with anxiety?
What forms of false trust appear today as oppression, wealth, public image or human influence?
How does the claim that God repays each one according to his work affects his way of living before him?
study.practice: Separate a moment of silence to repeat the central truths of the psalm with your own words: God is his rock, his salvation and his refuge. Then identify a concrete area in which you are supporting more heart in people, money, or control than in the Lord. Deliver this area in prayer, with sincerity, and practice during the week a specific decision of obedient trust, without feeding anxiety with murmuring or self-protection.
study.uncertainty: The exact historical context is not informed by the biblical text or by the notes. References to a possible political conflict, including an attempt to overthrow the king, are inferences of the commentators. There is also divergence in the notes on the meaning of some expressions of verse 1, but the axis of the psalm remains clear: submission and rest in God.
